newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX lower, Thyssen takeover rumours fly.
newsitem.headline: German DAX lower, Thyssen takeover rumours fly.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade lower on Tuesday, as this week's expiry of options on blue chip shares pressured prices and amid a flurry of rumours that steel maker Thyssen was poised to be taken over.
Shares in Thyssen and industrial group Krupp were both suspended from trade on Tuesday morning pending key announcements and banking sources said Krupp was poised to bid for all or part of Thyssen.
The news raised a storm on the German market, where hostile takeovers are rare and sent Thyssen shares soaring in unofficial trading -- the so-called grey market.

The broader blue chip DAX index eased after a solid start to begin bourse trade down 27.51 points at 3,323.48, as prices were impacted by the upcoming expiry of options contracts on the DAX and its constituents, a regular cause of volatility.
And dealers said there was still some concern about the risk of a hike in U.S. interest rates.
"But the real story, the only story, is the Thyssen takeover," one Frankfurt dealer said.

Engineering group Preussag AG benefited from the takeover talk, as dealers speculated about a capacity cut in its sector should Thyssen be amalgamated with Krupp. Its shares were up 7.50 marks at 437.50 marks in early bourse trade.
Thyssen, meanwhile, was trading at between 385 and 390 marks on the grey market, according to dealers, more than 10 percent over its all-time high. Its shares closed on Monday at 344.50 marks.
Chemical company Bayer AG was under pressure after releasing what dealers said were somewhat disappointing results and a stalled outlook for 1997 profit.
The shares were down 97 pfennigs at 70.85 marks.
